The plan

rule; its reasoning is recorded there.

Run 1 – Vedic Genesis (report: run-1.md)

Settled by the orchestrator (minor, under the user's standing rule): the run's six questions are rendering and
reading choices, each already translated with the defensible choice and the alternative in its note:

  1. AB niṣ-√krī פָּדָה and jyaiṣṭhya בכורה stay, tagged [equivalent] with Ex 13:13, 34:20: the comparison is
    the run's finding, and the tag says it is a shared motif, not a cognate (guidelines §6.4: do not hide a real parallel).
  2. Av. spəṇta נדיב stays (it avoids manufacturing Ps 51:13's רוח הקדושה).
  3. RV 10.190.3 yathāpūrvám "one after another" stays (the dictionaries); the cyclic reading stays in the note.
  4. The readings AB 7.13.1a "a king without a son", ŚB 1.2.3.9 "camel", KU 2.20b "the grace of the Arranger" stay,
    with the alternatives in the notes.
  5. RV 10.10.14d הסכמה טובה מאוד stays literal; its note already says the echo of Gen 1:31 is Hebrew-only.
  6. Av. dātar עושה against Skt dhātár הַמַּעֲמִיד: left to the lead's harmonization at the end of the round
    (the cross-language cognate question, guidelines §6.7).

No question from run 1 needs the user.

Run 2 – Hurro-Hittite myths (report: run-2.md)

Settled by the orchestrator (minor):

  1. SISKUR keeps the split by sense – מנחה in Ḫedammu (the gods' offerings from mankind), טקס in the rituals – as a
    recorded split; the lead's harmonization looks at it with the other Hittite splits.
  2. Appu's sons keep their names by meaning (רַע, יָשָׁר), as the Hittite hearer heard them (the speaking-names rule,
    guidelines §5.2, Hesiod); the transliteration stays in the note.

No question from run 2 needs the user.

Run 3 – Ugaritic epics and rituals (report: run-3.md)

No question for the user. The about 40 philological cruxes (uzr, mtm, npy …) are translated with a choice and the
alternative in the note, and listed under each tablet's "Open decisions" for the user's review of the drafts.

Run 4 – "Words in stone" (report: run-4.md)

For the user:

  1. Three key inscriptions wait for PDFs that only a browser can fetch. The open editions of Tell Fekheriye
    (CRAI 1981; Syria 1983 – the ṣlm / dmwt pair of Gen 1:26), Sefire (Dupont-Sommer and Starcky 1960; CRAI 1957)
    and Deir ʿAllā (Caquot and Lemaire, Syria 1977) are free to read on Persée, but its server refuses scripted
    downloads (403, then 500). If you save them from a browser into sources/ (the URLs are in
    sources/_records-only--Words-in-stone/README.md), a later round can translate them.
  2. Please confirm: a Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) transcription as an interim base text. The run used it for Mesad
    Hashavyahu, Ketef Hinnom II and the Gezer calendar, on the view that an openly licensed transcription of an ancient
    text is not "transcribing from a © book". Settled meanwhile by the orchestrator: accepted as an interim base, on
    the model of the Sargon Birth Legend on King 1907 – each project says it awaits a check against the critical edition.
    If you say no, those three become records-only (one script pass).

Settled by the orchestrator (minor): Sefire's ʿdy (not translated yet) is left to the run that does Sefire,
under the cross-language principles of guidelines §6.7; the echo tag on proper names ([cognate] when the name is the
same word, else [equivalent]) goes to the lead's harmonization at the end of this round.
